intended_object: The standard isomorphism M^μ ≅ Ind_{S_μ}^{S_n}(1): the Young permutation module of a partition μ of n (the permutation representation on μ-tabloids, i.e. on S_n/S_μ) is isomorphic to the trivial representation of the Young subgroup S_μ induced up to S_n. I took this from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition is the library's general isomorphism `TauCeti.indTrivialIso k H : Ind_H^G(trivial) ≅ k[G ⧸ H]`, taken at k = ℚ and H = youngSubgroup μ and then inverted. `indTrivialIso` is built with `Rep.mkIso`, which requires a G-equivariant linear equivalence, so the result really is an isomorphism in `Rep ℚ (S_n)`. Its source, `permutationModule μ`, is by definition `Rep.ofMulAction ℚ S_n (S_n ⧸ youngSubgroup μ)`, which is the Young permutation module M^μ. Its target is Mathlib's `Rep.ind` along the inclusion of the Young subgroup, applied to the trivial representation. So the type and the body match the classical statement M^μ ≅ Ind_{S_μ}^{S_n} 1.

The coefficient field is ℚ only because `permutationModule` is defined over ℚ. That choice belongs to that other definition, not to this one. The general version, over any field and for any subgroup, already exists in the library as `indTrivialIso`, so this declaration is just its specialization to Young subgroups and is not too narrow. On the formula `x ⊗ a ↦ single ⟦x⁻¹⟧ a`: the inverse is needed to make the map equivariant under Mathlib's convention for `Rep.ind`, and it does not affect correctness. I found no Mathlib declaration that gives this isomorphism.
